hints: Use the given frequency to find the period of one complete trace cycle.
Read the horizontal length of one full cycle from Fig. 5.1, then divide the period by that length in centimetres.
walkthrough: The sound frequency is f = 5000 Hz, so the period is T = 1/f = 1/5000 = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ s.
On the CRO trace, one complete cycle occupies 4.0 cm horizontally (equivalently, 1.5 cycles occupy 6.0 cm).
The time-base setting is time per centimetre: (2.0 × 10⁻⁴ s)/(4.0 cm).
Therefore, the time-base setting is 5.0 × 10⁻⁵ s cm⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the period as 1/5000 s = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ s.
Uses one cycle over 4.0 cm, or 1.5 cycles over 6.0 cm, to obtain 5.0 × 10⁻⁵ s cm⁻¹.

hints: The frequency is unchanged, so keep the horizontal spacing of the trace cycles unchanged.
Use I ∝ A² to find the new amplitude when the intensity is tripled; the original trace amplitude is 1.0 cm.
walkthrough: The frequency is unchanged, so the period and hence the horizontal spacing of the new CRO trace must match the original trace.
For a progressive wave, intensity is proportional to amplitude squared: I ∝ A².
Tripling the intensity gives A_new/A_old = √3. With A_old = 1.0 cm, A_new = √3 × 1.0 = 1.73... cm.
Sketch the same-period trace centred on the dashed line, with amplitude 1.7 cm from the centre line; it is therefore greater than 1.0 cm.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a new trace with the same period as the original trace.
Draws the new trace with amplitude greater than 1.0 cm.
Draws the new trace with amplitude approximately 1.7 cm from the centre line.

hints: Point P is the central point on the screen, so compare its distances from the two slits.
Use the path difference to decide the phase difference of the waves at P and hence the type of interference.
walkthrough: At the central point P, the two slits are the same distance from the screen point, so the path difference is zero.
A zero path difference gives a zero phase difference, so the waves arrive in phase.
The waves therefore interfere constructively, producing a bright fringe at P.
No major formula is required: the conclusion follows from equal paths and the constructive-interference condition.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the path difference or phase difference at P is zero and hence the interference is constructive.

hints: Use the double-slit fringe-spacing relation, with a as the slit separation and x as the adjacent-bright-fringe spacing.
Rearrange for D and convert the 630 nm wavelength to metres before substituting all three quantities.
walkthrough: For double-slit interference, λ = ax/D, where a is the slit separation and x is the fringe spacing.
Rearrange for the screen distance: D = ax/λ.
Convert the wavelength: λ = 630 nm = 630 × 10⁻⁹ m.
Therefore, D = 2.3 m.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the double-slit relation λ = ax/D.
Rearranges to D = ax/λ and substitutes the slit separation, fringe spacing and wavelength in metres.
Calculates the screen distance as 2.3 m, or an equivalent correctly rounded value.

hints: Rearrange the double-slit relation so fringe spacing x is expressed in terms of wavelength λ.
The graph begins at λ = 400 nm rather than zero, so decide whether x is zero or positive at the left edge of the plotted range.
walkthrough: The double-slit relation is λ = ax/D, which rearranges to x = (D/a)λ.
D and a are unchanged, so D/a is constant and x is directly proportional to λ.
Therefore, draw an upward-sloping straight line over the plotted wavelength range.
At λ = 400 nm, the wavelength is already positive, so x is also positive; the line starts above zero at the left edge of the graph.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws an upward-sloping straight line that starts at a non-zero fringe spacing at λ = 400 nm.
